rationale: bugs_open/342, filed 2026-08-20 at the council's own request (trail a44d9eb8: bug_historian's GATING objection, architecture's round-2 advisory 'worth a follow-up ticket'), taken up on the owner's instruction 2026-08-21 after checking nobody else owns it (who-owns.py: only the filing commit; no open work item; json_envelope.go untouched by any other lane). THE DEFECT. Go's text/template runs with Option("missingkey=zero"), so a field the template references and the content never supplied renders as EMPTY WITH NO ERROR. Page assembly then drops the visually-empty section, so the content does not arrive broken — it does not arrive at all. That is the mechanism behind this estate's recorded fleet-wide blanking of article bodies (bugs_closed/004/005) and 016b §9 carries it as a live pattern. THE COVERAGE, measured rather than asserted: missingRequiredLLMFields (json_envelope.go) is the gate that catches it, and it was called from exactly TWO of the FIFTEEN render call sites — v3_site_actions.go (build) and rerender_page_sections_action.go (rerender pre-check) — and even there only for fields the schema marks BOTH source:llm AND required. Thirteen sites had nothing, including both section-editor routes that write rendered_html straight to an already-live page. THE FIX, which is RFC_041 §5's candidate (a) — the structural one, chosen over candidate (b) 'call the existing gate at the other thirteen sites' because that is thirteen edits that still leave optional fields and schema-less components uncovered and still depends on each caller remembering. The RenderContext now carries the component's InputSchema, and the SEAM applies the rule for every caller. It is the SAME function the two pre-render gates call, deliberately not a second implementation of 'required' and 'empty' — one rule, one place, so the seam and the pre-check cannot drift about what those words mean. REPORT ONLY, NO REFUSAL, and that is the load-bearing scoping decision. Refusing at the seam would be new authority over content that renders successfully today at thirteen sites that never asked for it (owner ruling 2026-08-02 §2), and the two paths that DO want to refuse already do, before the render, where refusing is cheaper and the item is parked rather than failed. What this closes is the SILENCE, which is 342's actual complaint and its title. Error, not Warn: the sibling reports in the same block are Warn for a merely-empty optional field and Error for a dead URL control, and a required field whose section is about to be dropped belongs with the latter. REUSE, NOT ADDITION: the schema does not arrive as a new field. RenderContext already had SchemaSnapshot ('the locked input_schema, only used in strict mode') plus SchemaMode and a RenderOptions struct — all three DEAD since bugs_closed/260 deleted their only reader, RenderTemplateWithValidation, with the regex fallback. They are removed and the slot is repurposed under an honest name. So this change deletes three declarations that described a strict-mode validation the binary had stopped doing, and adds one that describes what it now does. A FINDING THE TESTS FORCED OUT, which a reviewer should look at hardest: the seam and the pre-render gate give DIFFERENT ANSWERS on the same content, and both are correct. The seam judges `data` — the merged map the template actually sees — and contextToInterfaceMap supplies fleet defaults there (cta_text falls back to 'Get Started'), so a required field the writer never produced can still render something. The pre-render gate judges the writer's ContentData and refuses on that. They are asking different questions: 'did the WRITER supply it?' versus 'will it RENDER EMPTY?', and 342's damage is the second one. The seam's report is therefore a strict SUBSET of the gate's. I did not design that; the first version of the test asserted the two lists were equal, failed, and named cta_text. It is now pinned as a test with the reason in it, and stated at the seam, so the next reader does not 'fix' one to match the other. CONTROL-FIELD SAFETY: InputSchema is a control field — content that could set it would be handing the renderer its own contract and switching off its own check. It is a map, and the step contract is derived by reflection over STRING fields only, so it is excluded from both the template map and the step boundary STRUCTURALLY rather than by a list entry. The test that guarded schema_mode for exactly this reason now guards InputSchema (same property, better subject), and renderContextControlFields is left deliberately EMPTY with a comment saying why, rather than carrying a stale entry for a deleted field.

plan.summary: Close bugs_open/342's SILENCE at all fifteen render call sites by carrying the component's declared schema on the RenderContext and having the seam apply missingRequiredLLMFields — the same function the two pre-render gates call — logging absent required fields at Error. No refusal is added anywhere: refusing at the seam would be new authority over content that renders today, and the two paths that want to refuse already do it before the render. The schema field REPLACES three dead declarations (SchemaSnapshot, SchemaMode, RenderOptions) whose only reader went with the regex fallback in bugs_closed/260. Nine call sites now pass a schema (build, chrome store, rerender, library assembly, and the three chrome renderers); the rest pass nil, which means UNKNOWN and reports nothing — fail-open, stated, and tested. Six tests including three CONTROLS (complete content silent, optional-absent silent, nil-schema silent) and one that pins a genuine divergence between the seam and the pre-render gate; mutation-proven by disabling the report, which fails two of them.

edits.rationale: The whole change. The seam is where all fifteen callers arrive, so it is where a guarantee can be made mechanical instead of left to each caller remembering — the same move as the existing form_action seeding and InstanceID report in this very function, and the reason candidate (a) beat candidate (b).

edits.symbol: six tests, three of them controls
edits.rationale: A log-only change is exactly the kind that ships inert, so the report is asserted through a zap observer rather than eyeballed. The controls carry more weight than the positive case: a report that also fires on healthy renders is noise, and noise on every page is how a real signal gets filtered out by whoever reads the logs.
edits.sketch: TestAbsentRequiredFieldIsReported (the defect) · TestCompleteContentIsSilent · TestAbsentOptionalFieldIsNotReportedAsRequired (optional-absent is already covered at Warn; escalating it would erase the distinction) · TestNoSchemaMeansNoReport (nil = UNKNOWN, thirteen sites pass nil today) · TestRequiredNonLLMFieldIsNotTheSeamsBusiness (a resolver fill is reported by the fill path with more context) · TestSeamReportsASubsetOfThePreRenderGateAndSaysWhy (the divergence, with the reason in the failure message). The helper reads the field via entry.ContextMap(), not a type assertion on Field.Interface — zap.Strings stores an ArrayMarshaler, so the assertion silently yields nil, which reads exactly like 'the report named no fields'. The first version did that and the test caught it.

Chrome store. It already parses input_schema for the data-source fill, so this only lifts the parsed map to function scope — the same reason `unresolved` is already at function scope in that function.

plan.risks: 1) THE REPORT IS A LOG LINE, AND THIS ESTATE'S OWN RULING IS THAT 'A NAMED LOG IS NOT ESCALATION' (bugs_open/054, owner 2026-07-22). Stated plainly rather than dressed up: this makes 342 AUDIBLE at fifteen sites, it does not make it ACTIONED anywhere. The honest next step is a per-path decision about refusal or a work item, and it is deliberately not in this change because refusal at the seam is new authority. 2) Nine of fifteen sites pass a schema; six pass nil and therefore report nothing. That is fail-open and it is tested (TestNoSchemaMeansNoReport), but a reader must not take 'the seam covers every caller' to mean 'every caller supplies the contract'. The offline audit is deliberately NOT wired because it probes with fields removed on purpose. 3) The FLAT chrome schema shape gets no field set from SchemaContentFields, so those slots are silent — noted in the code where it happens. 4) Log volume: the report fires per render on affected sections. On today's estate it fires only where a required field is genuinely absent, which is by construction a build that is already going wrong; if it turns out to be chatty, that is evidence about content quality rather than about the check, and the fix is upstream. 5) Deleting SchemaMode/SchemaSnapshot/RenderOptions is a small API removal in a shared package: they are unexported-in-effect (nothing outside this package referenced them, verified by grep across platform/ and cmd/), but a lane holding an uncommitted branch that sets SchemaMode would now fail to compile. 6) No DB change, no config key, no migration, nothing to arm, and the change is inert until the next chassis roll.
